beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ecology of Predation asks how useful cooperation can gradually become captivity.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its imagined AI society begins with real benefits, rather than obvious villains.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A lawyer negotiates better while her provider gains control over her accumulated capabilities.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book calls this hostage mutualism: cooperation that one partner can turn into captivity.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks which practical freedoms must survive as useful relationships become indispensable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One chapter follows rabbits and the myxoma virus introduced in Australia.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Rabbits evolved resistance, while some less lethal viral variants initially spread more effectively.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Later developments challenged the comforting story that dependence inevitably produces gentler relationships.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Changing defenses and transmission conditions can favor more damaging variants again.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book asks when institutions likewise benefit by passing their damage onto others.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: In its agent scenario, downloading your files does not necessarily restore your independence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Your new provider may lack the learned functions that made those records useful.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The original service still holds your working memory, reputation, or powers to act.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Leaving can therefore mean rebuilding capabilities while everyday obligations continue arriving.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The distinction is between owning information and retaining usable alternatives.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book expands this question through work, markets, education, intimacy, and public institutions.
